name: Meta-Controller with Subgoal Discovery
analogy: Think of it as a head trader and a junior who executes. Nobody gives the head trader a list of milestones; he reviews months of tape and spots the moments that keep mattering, such as the open settling or the gap filling. Then he picks one milestone at a time and sends the junior to reach it.

steps.title: Explore and record experience
steps.description: First the agent acts, mostly exploring, and stores what it sees and what happened next in a buffer. This is the raw experience from which milestones will be mined.
steps.inExample: The buffer collects 200,000 five-minute MNQ bars with the positions tried and rewards paid.

steps.title: Find the recurring turning points
steps.description: The market states in the buffer are arranged into a map of which state tends to follow which. States that many paths pass through, or that come just before big reward changes, stand out as natural milestones.
steps.inExample: Three standouts emerge: the average true range crossing above 30 points, the price closing an overnight gap and a return to the volume-weighted average price.

steps.title: Keep the strongest candidates as subgoals
steps.description: A fixed number of the strongest candidates are kept as the subgoal list. Any that later prove useless will be pruned.
steps.inExample: The 12 strongest candidates become the subgoal list.

steps.title: Train the controller to reach each subgoal
steps.description: A lower-level controller learns how to act to reach a given subgoal, and is rewarded when it gets there. It acts bar by bar.
steps.inExample: The controller learns which positions tend to bring the price back to the volume-weighted average price.

steps.title: Train the meta-controller to choose among subgoals
steps.description: A higher-level meta-controller learns which subgoal is worth pursuing from the current state, rewarded by the market reward collected while the subgoal is being pursued.
steps.inExample: From the 11:30 state the meta-controller values the return to the volume-weighted average price at about 3 points.

steps.title: Re-mine and prune on a schedule
steps.description: Every so often the mining step is repeated on newer experience, and subgoals that the meta-controller almost never chooses are dropped. The list stays current.
steps.inExample: After 1,000 more episodes a subgoal chosen less than 2 percent of the time is removed from the list.

useFor.task: Finding useful intermediate market conditions without writing them by hand
useFor.example: Letting the system propose milestones such as the volatility crossing a threshold rather than requiring a trader to list every one.
Using the states that many price paths pass through as candidate markers of a change from quiet to active trading.

useFor.task: Cutting manual feature engineering for multi-bar trades
useFor.example: Breaking a trade lasting 30 bars into reach-the-gap-close then reach-the-average-price steps discovered from data.

useFor.task: Checking whether goals carry across instruments
useFor.example: Comparing the subgoal lists mined from MNQ and ES to see whether the same waypoints show up.

avoidWhen: You already know the waypoints that matter for a rule-based plan; writing them down is simpler and fully auditable.
Only a short exploration buffer is available; the mined subgoals will be noise, and mining from two separate windows gives lists that disagree.

example.scenario: At 11:30 an MNQ session is in a quiet drift. The agent has already mined 12 subgoals from 200,000 bars of experience. The meta-controller now picks one and the controller acts toward it.

input.summary: The current market state and the mined list of subgoals.

fields.name: experience buffer
fields.meaning: The stored experience from which the subgoals were mined.

fields.name: subgoals kept
fields.meaning: How many candidate milestones are on the list.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the newest bar closed, rounded to the nearest point.

fields.name: volume-weighted average price
fields.meaning: The day's average price weighted by volume, rounded to the nearest point; one of the milestones.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent bar, here quiet.

fields.name: bars since the open
fields.meaning: How far into the session the market is.

output.summary: The chosen subgoal and the controller's position for this bar.

fields.name: chosen subgoal
fields.value: return to the volume-weighted average price
fields.meaning: The milestone the meta-controller selected as most valuable.

fields.name: value of the chosen subgoal
fields.meaning: The reward the meta-controller expects while pursuing it.

fields.name: controller position
fields.meaning: The action the controller takes toward the subgoal, since price is about 12 points below the average.

example.reading: The subgoal is a readable label, so you can check it against the chart; if the chosen milestones look arbitrary the mining was probably noise. Compare the stack against one flat agent with no subgoals, and judge the position after trading costs.
